title: Posting: one program per setup, or an optional stop between setups

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while programming a small two-sided part with HAT-style stock and soft jaws (user's project), with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (macOS arm64), driven headlessly over MCP, Tormach PathPilot post.

## What happens

A document with two setups (Setup 1 at G54, Setup 2 at G55, with the part flipped between them) posts as **one program**. Setup 2's first operation follows Setup 1's last move with **no program stop** (`M0`/`M1`) and no message to the operator. From the posted file:

```
G1 X1.3127 Y-1.0908 Z-0.2962 F30
G0 X1.3127 Y-1.0908 Z0.9843
M9
M5
(SETUP: Setup 2)
(OPERATION: S2 Face hat off rough - FACE - G55)
G17 G90 G55 G40 G49 G80
...
T31 M6
G43 H31
S9500 M3
M8
```

On cycle start, the machine finishes Setup 1 and **starts cutting Setup 2's path at once**, before anyone has flipped or re-clamped the part. Setup 2's program is then running on a part still clamped for Setup 1. It cuts air at best; at worst it cuts the wrong side of the part, the vise or the parallels at full feed.

To get one program per setup, the user had to delete the other setup's ops from a scratch copy and post again, or cut the file apart by hand.

A per-operation "after" action already exists (`AfterOperation`: optional stop / program stop / go home, #110), and a program-stop entry can be put after an op in the GUI. **Nothing puts one at a setup boundary by default**, and I found no MCP tool that adds a stop entry.

## Expected

The user chooses, per document (and in the post dialog / MCP `post`), between:

1. **one file per setup** (for example `name_setup1.nc`, `name_setup2.nc`, each with its own header, tool list, work offset and `M30`); or
2. **one file with a stop between setups**: an `M0` (or `M1` if the user prefers) after the last op of each setup, with a comment naming the next setup and what to do (`(SETUP 2: FLIP PART, CLAMP ..., G55)`).

**Safety:** the default for a multi-setup document posted as one file should be the `M0` stop, not "run straight on". A program that moves from one setup to the next with no pause is a crash waiting for an operator who expects it to stop. The current default may deserve a higher priority than this issue carries.

**Done means:** posting a two-setup document either writes one file per setup, or writes one file with an `M0` and a setup-change comment between the setups, as chosen. With no choice made, the default never runs from one setup into the next without a stop. The MCP `post` tool takes the choice. A pinning post test covers both modes on at least the Fanuc and Tormach dialects.

Related: #110 (per-operation after-action), #388 (one file per post when setups use different machines), #258 (post dialog options).
